texts.preamble: Raj Kumar vs State Of Punjab on 30 January, 2025 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:014385 256 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh Crr-661-2012 Date of decision: 30.01.2025 Raj Kumar ...Petitioner V/S State Of Punjab ...Respondent Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Harpreet Singh Brar Present: Mr. B.S. Mamli, Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. Nitesh Sharma, Dag, Punjab. ** ** Harpreet Singh Brar, J. (Oral) 1.
texts.facts: 2. Brief facts of the case of prosecution are that Doctor Nirmal Singh working as Medical Officer at Mini PHC, Karandi PHC, Sardulgarh was appointed as Food Inspector Inspector for the entire area of State of Punjab vide government notification No.5204-2 No.5204 -76/14111 76/14111 dated 30th April 1976 under Section 9 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was also authorized to launch criminal proceedings thereof DHS vide letter No. E-7(1) 7(1) 1 of 4 Neutral Citation Raj Kumar vs State Of Punjab on 30 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102951521/ 1 No:=2025:PHHC:014385 CRR-661-2012 Pb., 2004/2848 dated 29.6.2004. On 15.12.2005 at about 10 10-00 a.m., he, in the presence of Doctor Rupinder Kumar, SMO Incharge Khiala Kalan, Mansa intercepted one Raj Kumar (petitioner herein) son of Sh. Diwan Chand at Karandi Bus Stand. The person person was on Rajdoot Motor cycle having without number plate and was in possession of about 160 liters of mixed milk of cows and buffaloes in four drums kept for sale for human consumption as confessed by him. He (complainant) after disclosing his identity aas Food Inspector to the petitioner, demanded a sample of milk by giving giving him a notice vide form No. No.VI VI prescribed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1954, same was also signed by the petitioner and witnessed by Sat Pal Pharmacist, PHC, Sardulgarh, District Mansa and he himself. When the sample of milk was sent to Local Health Authority, Mansa it was declared as adulterated and unfit for human consumption in the report. report. Hence, the complaint.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the Courts below have not appreciated the evidence properly and the trial Court has given undue weightage to the evidence of the prosecution. Further, no independent witness was joined or examined by the prosecution prosecution.. He submits that mandatory provisions of the Act were also not followed by the complainant as he failed to send any intimation to the petitioner regarding the analysis report for giving him choice to get the sample analysist second time. Learned counsel further submits that the link evidence is missing as there is no affidavit of the person, who took the sample to the Chemical Examiner Laboratory. Furthermore, there is unexplained delay in filing the complaint. 4. Per contra, contra, learned State counsel opposes the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner and submits that the petitioner has been convicted by the learned trial Court based on correct appreciation of the facts 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:014385 CRR-661-2012 and the law. Moreover, the conviction has been upheld by the learned lower Appellate Court, as such interference by this this Court is not warranted. A two Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Som Dutt and others Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh (2022) 6 SCC 722 speaking through Justice Be Bela la M. Trivedi, has held as under:- "6....having regard to the fact there are no criminal antecedents against the appellants, the court is inclined to give them the benefit of releasing them on probation of good conduct. In that view of the matter, while maintaining the conviction and senten sentence ce imposed on the appellants, it is Raj Kumar vs State Of Punjab on 30 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102951521/ 2 directed that the appellants shall be released on probation of good conduct....." A two Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Lakhvir Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2021) 2 SCC 763 speaking through Justice Sanjay Kishan ishan Kaul, has held as under:- under: "6. We may notice that the Statement of Objects and Reasons of the said Act explains the rationale for the enactment and its amendments: to give the benefit of release of offenders on probation of good conduct instead of se sentencing ntencing them to imprisonment. Thus, increasing emphasis on the reformation and rehabilitation of offenders as useful and self self-reliant reliant members of 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:014385 CRR-661-2012 society without subjecting them to the deleterious effects of jail life is what is sought to be subserved." 6.
